messages:
Riley: Noticing followups are piling up again. Proposal: add a short 'claim window' policy + a lightweight escalation ticket so things don't drift. Thoughts?
Nora: Agree. We should avoid manual chasing. What's the claim window you had in mind?
Riley: 72h by default, 24h for P0/P1. If unclaimed, bot creates an escalation ticket assigned to oncall-leads and posts a summary in #eng-oncall.
Diego: +1. Also require a 1-line verification note when closing (how you validated fix). Cuts fuzzy closures.
Asha: Can we add a recurrence flag on actions to mark repeating failure modes? That can bump priority automatically.
incident-bot: Note: I can create escalation tickets and post digests. Need a JQL template for overdue items.
Riley: JQL example: `project = PM AND status != Done AND due_date < now()` — bot can use that. Also add `AND recurrence = true` for pattern scans.
Nora: Process ask: remediation_owner must be assigned in postmortem or within claim window; IC should not be auto-owner. Prevents role blur.
Diego: For visibility, weekly heatmap that shows unclaimed_count, median_time_to_claim, percent_overdue. Two-week pilot to validate impact.
Asha: I'll run the pilot coordination (schedule, calendar). Riley, can you handle the bot config?
Riley: Yep, I'll wire the JQL and create the digest. incident-bot: please ping when ready.
incident-bot: Scheduled: digest job and escalation ticket flow queued.
Nora: Small UX: when an escalation ticket is created, DM top-3 oncall eligibles with a one-click claim link. Cuts friction.
Riley: Good idea. We'll prototype for the pilot. Start Monday, review after 2 weeks.
Diego: Sounds good. Goal: reduce unclaimed followups to <5% and make closures objective.
Asha: Closing thread; will post pilot timeline and invites.
